text:
Alex: Heads up — after yesterday's adaptive-batcher change I see periodic 20-40ms spikes on short sequences. nsys traces attached. Anyone else?
Mira: saw that in canary, suspected kselector churn when batch sizes drop. dump?
Alex: uploading two traces: /artifacts/traces/nsys/batch_throttle_before.qdrep and /artifacts/traces/nsys/batch_throttle_after.qdrep
Sam: quick note: before = commit e3a4b9f, after = d1c7f2a (adaptive-batcher + kselector weight tweak)
PerfBot: nsys summary for before: GPU time 58ms/event, kernel switch count 12, avg small-kernel-latency 0.9ms
PerfBot: nsys summary for after: GPU time 74ms/event, kernel switch count 18, avg small-kernel-latency 1.6ms
Mira: that's a 27% regression in GPU time and 50% more kernel switches. Could be prefetch + kselector racing.
Lee: can you paste the perfetto flame links? want timeline with CPU->CUDA boundaries.
Alex: perfetto links: https://perfetto.local/trace/abc123 (before) and https://perfetto.local/trace/def456 (after)
Sam: quick diff I ran:
```
# extract kernel timeline
nsys report --format csv --report cpu,gpu --input before.qdrep > before.csv
nsys report --format csv --report cpu,gpu --input after.qdrep > after.csv
python tools/trace_diff.py before.csv after.csv --metric kernel-switches
```
Sam: biggest delta in small GEMM (sgemm_batched) and prefetch memcpy kernels during batch handoff
Mira: hypothesis: new batch-throttle makes more tiny batches -> more frequent warmup kernels, kselector toggles to conservative kernels
Alex: can we reproduce with a run that forces single-sequence short batches? I have a repro script.
Lee: trying now, running 50k short seqs with logging ON
PerfBot: run finished, sample log snippet:
```
[2024-05-02T13:10:23Z] seq=1 batch=1 kernel=warmup_gemm 0.8ms
[2024-05-02T13:10:23Z] seq=2 batch=1 kernel=prefetch_memcpy 1.2ms
[2024-05-02T13:10:23Z] seq=3 batch=1 kernel=sgemm_small 1.1ms
```
Mira: looks like prefetch is now being scheduled more often. Could add aggregation window or bump warmup threshold.
Alex: if we bisect, the candidate commit that introduced throttle logic is e3a4b9f -> d1c7f2a; can someone run quick git-bisect with perf trace check?
Sam: I kicked off a quick bisect script that builds at each head and runs 1000 sequences; results: regression introduced by d1c7f2a in kselector weight handling
Mira: proposed fix: debounce kernel-choice signals for 50ms and prefer previous kernel until batch size > N
Lee: wrote small patch and ran perf: GPU time dropped back to 60ms/event and kernel switches back to 13
Alex: awesome. Can we roll this as canary revert plus patch? Also add unit test for weight smoothing and a perf regression test harness.
Sam: filing PR 4823 with revert+patch, adding trace asserts. Assigning reviewers @Mira @Lee
Mira: ack, I'll review today :+1:
Alex: thanks all, leaving traces and diffs in the ticket.
